diagrams.title: The reconstruction questions
diagrams.caption: A collision, an action on a representation and a measurement in a prepared state each supply a test of boundary reconstruction. The links place the corresponding questions in the book.

nodes.label: Fields at colliding points
nodes.description: A residue measures singular behaviour at a collision. A coefficient supported there can disappear on the open set of distinct points.

nodes.label: Products and higher relations
nodes.description: Bar records multiplication by contracting adjacent factors. Cobar recovers a connected algebra through the finite filtration by word length.

nodes.label: Modules and interface maps
nodes.description: A module is recovered when the unit of the interface adjunction is invertible on it. The counit tests recovery on the other side.

nodes.label: Actions and vacuum evaluation
nodes.description: Evaluation sends an action to a character. Recognition asks whether multiplication by that character recovers the entire pointed action.

nodes.label: Inputs for repeated operations
nodes.description: Collecting coefficients in one Laurent series and forming an algebraic tensor with a spectator impose different finiteness conditions.

nodes.label: Fields and coproducts
nodes.description: A coproduct gives an action on two representations. In the spectral example the two levels combine in order and the tensor carries a cross contraction.

nodes.label: Vacua and collision extensions
nodes.description: Ordinary geometric reconstruction uses the family of realized vacua and its maps over every marked configuration.

nodes.label: Composition of junctions
nodes.description: Derived tensor product retains both outer actions. For particle junctions it also detects a degree-two flux class.

nodes.label: Extensions and compact states
nodes.description: A Hall product uses the space of extensions. A compact three-point operation can distinguish products whose prescribed traces agree.

nodes.label: Weil traces and local fields
nodes.description: An arithmetic operator realizes the full Weil functional. Global positivity asks for the sign of its values on convolution squares.

nodes.label: States and filling amplitudes
nodes.description: A normalized state gives expectations. Absolute amplitudes also require a choice of normalization for the integration and its sewing.

nodes.label: The physical bulk
nodes.description: Bulk reconstruction compares independently defined fields and states with their boundary actions, collision maps and measurements.

diagrams.title: The representation comparison within reconstruction
diagrams.caption: The unit recovers modules on the specified affine source. Comparing the tensor product of two such modules with the fusion of their physical lines requires a map for that operation.

diagrams.title: Combining representations requires the local operations
diagrams.caption: The coproduct in the spectral construction combines two levels. Its compatibility with the fields uses both the exchange and the cross contraction in their tensor product.

diagrams.title: A full trace and a positive local theory are different targets
diagrams.caption: The full Weil trace determines a distribution. Its sign on convolution squares is a further question. Compact three-point products give a geometric example in which prescribed traces agree while the products differ.

diagrams.title: What must survive reconstruction
diagrams.caption: Physical reconstruction compares a bulk observable with its boundary action and a prescribed filling with a prepared state. In the Gaussian example a neutral ray pair and a linearly sourced harmonic disk give the same normalized oscillator law.

diagrams.title: The support detected by consecutive cuts
diagrams.caption: A point outside both separating opens has \(x_1=x_3\). The middle point can lie elsewhere, so the common complement is the whole diagonal \(\Delta_{13}\).
hypotheses: Smooth curve; external input order 1,2,3; only consecutive cuts.

witness.conclusion: Both consecutive cuts fail, although the point is outside the small diagonal.

diagrams.title: Bar and cobar retain the ordered operations
diagrams.caption: The empty coefficient is \(k\). On \(n\) labels there are at most \(n\) positive factors. This finite bound proves that bar and cobar are inverse on connected objects, including unbounded complexes.

nodes.label: Connected counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras

relations.text: The two functors are inverse equivalences, including the full mapping spaces.
The intrinsic adjunction is \(B\dashv\Omega\); the strict twisting-cochain adjunction has the opposite presentation \(\Omega_{\rm dg}\dashv B_{\rm dg}\).

hypotheses: Smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field.
Ordinary unbounded right differential-module complexes with the consecutive-cut convolution.
Empty coefficient identified with k; all higher associativity and coassociativity data retained.

diagrams.title: Four inflated factors recover an arbitrary source
diagrams.caption: For \(B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\) with \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), the tower runs from zero to the ordinary unbounded complex \(L\). Each two-arrow row begins a cofiber triangle. The displayed unit \(u\) comes from scalar extension. The realization has its own unit \(\eta\).

nodes.label: \(UF(T_0(L))\)
nodes.description: Inflated from the unrestricted R-complex obtained by derived scalar extension.

nodes.label: \(UF(T_1(L))\)
nodes.description: Inflated from the unrestricted R-complex obtained by derived scalar extension.

nodes.label: \(UF(T_2(L))\)
nodes.description: Inflated from the unrestricted R-complex obtained by derived scalar extension.

nodes.label: \(UF(T_3(L))\)
nodes.description: Inflated from the unrestricted R-complex obtained by derived scalar extension.

hypotheses: \(R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), \(I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w\), and \(F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\); \(U\) is inflation.
Both R-actions and two-sided K-flatness are retained.
\(I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}4}=0\), while \(I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}3}\ne0\).

relations.text: Under the separately stated smooth realization hypotheses, invertibility of its actual unit on inflated complexes propagates through this finite tower.

diagrams.title: From a character to an action, and back to the vacuum
diagrams.caption: Multiplication followed by vacuum evaluation gives \(\Psi\Theta\simeq1\). On the recognized families the opposite composite also recovers the pointing homotopy and its higher compatibilities. The genuine Heisenberg example leads to an automorphism problem.

relations.text: \(\Theta\Psi\simeq1\) on the genuinely unital Chevalley family, its specified module extensions, and the nonunital families of Chapter 7.
Full recognition for every pointed factorizing actor, with all roots and refinements.

hypotheses: Characteristic-zero field; the ordered collision category and both tensors specified in Chapter 7.
\(C\) is the Chevalley coalgebra of \(kp_1\oplus kp_2\); \(u\) is an actual coherent pointing.
prohibitions: An equivalence for every pointed factorizing actor remains open.
The ordinary exterior-source mapping space uses a different category and has its own presentation.

diagrams.title: The two coproduct paths give the same three-system action
diagrams.caption: The two paths have the same three-system action in the tensor \(\boxtimes_\rho\), which includes the cross contraction. The order of levels is fixed even when their group is noncommutative.
hypotheses: Flat Hopf algebra with bijective antipode over a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra.
Translation, unitary spectral coquasitriangular form and level automorphisms satisfy all displayed identities in Chapter 12.
The fields and all finite products have the specified common rational germs and expansion domains.

diagrams.title: Extension multiplication retains its middle geometry
diagrams.caption: The left map sends an extension to its quotient and subobject. The right map sends it to its middle object. For constructible functions, integration over the fibre of \(q\) sums the pulled-back values. Critical coefficients require an oriented map on this correspondence.
hypotheses: The constructible-function integral uses finite charge support and an actual domain on which Euler integration is defined.
The coefficient-complex formula is additional data on its specified critical/oriented correspondence; its shifts, supports and orientation roots are retained.
diagrams.status: Ordinary Hall multiplication and the oriented coefficient comparison

diagrams.title: The full trace and the positive critical trace differ by an exact remainder
diagrams.caption: The critical-line representation contributes with the full multiplicity of each of its zeros. The remaining distribution is the sum over nonreal centred zeros. Its vanishing on every test is a global assertion.

edges.label: Trace of the positive critical representation

relations.text: The decomposition is exact on the stated test algebra.

relations.status: Open problem equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis

prohibitions: The nonreal remainder is not known to vanish on every test.
A complex-bilinear residue dual is different from a positive Hilbert pairing.

diagrams.title: A normalized state, an amplitude line and a filling
diagrams.caption: On the solid torus, finite cycles give normalized correlations and coefficient heat supplies a based local amplitude. Comparing either construction with a prescribed gravitational filling requires its actual cycle, observable map and spatial sewing.

nodes.label: Original finite singular-window cycle integrals
nodes.description: The same singular-pair Gaussian coordinates couple all windows. The integration uses the transported cycles and every odd variable.

nodes.label: Normalized numerical state \(\omega_\mu\)
nodes.description: Radon even Gaussian law and full graded Wick moments on the specified observable space.

nodes.label: Original finite coefficient action lines and coefficient heat
nodes.description: Reflected fixed-adjoint realization, finite Riesz action blocks and continued density-cycle frames.

nodes.label: Based local section \(s_{\mathrm{fp}}\) of the vacuum line
nodes.description: Integration over finite shells and the heat finite part retain the base amplitude and the connection.

nodes.label: State and amplitude prepared by the prescribed filling
nodes.description: A gravitational filling specifies its boundary state space, observable comparison, amplitude line and cutting and gluing maps.

edges.label: Normalize and take the proved cycle limit
hypotheses: Fixed metric and density; 0<|q|<1, κ≠0, ħ>0.
Smooth integrable μ with zero normal trace in the stated small inverse neighbourhood; supplied smooth Ward filling Tμ.
Original coupled finite cycles and the declared test-observable topology.

edges.label: Finite shell maps and the original heat finite part
hypotheses: Original reflected weighted realization with the stated spectral gap and C⁴/C¹-small source bounds.
Higher-seminorm bounds for source derivatives; integrability and smooth Ward filling for action-line statements.
Local source neighbourhood; original base action integral retained.

Identify the amplitude line and gluing normalization

prohibitions: Normalizing cancels an overall scalar in a fixed fibre.
